title: anatomy
description: A rest anatomy for the musculoskeletal solver: the base model whose skeleton it builds on, the tissue surfaces over it, how tissue attaches to bone, the ligament and tendon rods, and the body parameters a run may set. Written by the anatomy authoring side, read by the solver (REFACTOR/ANATOMY_EXCHANGE.md); the skeleton itself is the base model's and is never copied here.

$schema.description: The schema this document follows, by its `$id`: the last path segment names the file in husk's schema/ directory, and schema_version says which version of it (REFACTOR/BUNDLE_FORMAT.md "The contract header").

schema_version.description: Version of the anatomy family's schemas this document conforms to. The family has its own version line, apart from the WoW kinds' (REFACTOR/ANATOMY_EXCHANGE.md invariant 6).

subject.description: The anatomy, by the name its author gave it; it has no identity of its own.

space.description: Units and axes of every value in the document: metres, as in the base model.

provenance.description: Who wrote it, from what: input_format names the authoring tool's export.

definition.description: What the anatomy is made of, at rest.

base_model.description: The musculoskeletal model the anatomy builds on: its bodies, joints, joint ranges and muscle-tendon paths. Referenced, not copied, so kinematics has one source (REFACTOR/ANATOMY_EXCHANGE.md invariant 1); every `body`, `base_muscle` and `base_tendon` below is a name in it.

model.description: The model file. Its media type by convention is model/vnd.mujoco.mjcf+xml, a MuJoCo MJCF file, which is what the solver loads.

name.description: The model's published name, e.g. MS-Human-700.

revision.description: Which published state of the model the file is: a commit, tag or release.

licence.description: The model's licence, as an SPDX identifier where one exists.

tissues.description: Every soft-tissue volume, each a closed surface at rest. The solver meshes tets from these surfaces, so none are stored.

id.description: The tissue's name, unique among the tissues.

layer.description: Which anatomical layer the tissue is. Exactly one tissue is skin: the fixed skin topology every result is over (REFACTOR/ANATOMY_EXCHANGE.md invariant 4).

surface.description: The tissue's closed, outward-facing polygon surface at rest, faces in the authoring tool's own order so per-face results land on its faces by index. A quad list, not strips: strip order can't keep that face order, and a GPU strip layout is the consumer's to build.

positions.description: Vertex positions, f32 x 3 per vertex, metres, in the base model's rest frame.

face_sizes.description: Corners per face, u8 x 1 per face, at least 3; the skin's at least 4 (no triangles: the skin is the quad base mesh that Multires and the quad GPU path work on).

face_vertices.description: Every face's corners in face order, u32 x 1 per corner, indices into positions, counter-clockwise seen from outside; a face's corners start where the previous faces' sizes sum to.

edges.description: The surface's edges, u32 x 2 per edge (two indices into positions), in the authoring tool's own edge order, which faces can't reproduce; required on the skin, whose per-edge stretch results are over it.

base_muscle.description: A muscle tissue's muscle in the base model, whose path seeds the tissue's medial axis. Absent for a muscle the base model doesn't have (a tail muscle) and for fat and skin.

fibre_directions.description: A muscle's fibre direction per surface vertex, f32 x 3, unit length, in the rest frame; required for muscles, absent otherwise. The solver interpolates it into the tets.

attachments.description: Tissue bound to bone: the listed vertices of a tissue follow a base-model body rigidly (a muscle's origin and insertion, fat or skin bound over bone).

items.description: One tissue's vertices bound to one body.

id.description: The attachment's name, unique among the attachments.

body.description: The base-model body it is attached to.

vertices.description: The attached vertices, u32 x 1 each, indices into the tissue's surface positions.

rods.description: Ligaments and tendons, simulated as rods between two ends. A ligament's stiffness is set by the ligament laxity parameter, so joint limits emerge from it rather than from clamps.

id.description: The rod's name, unique among the rods.

role.description: What the rod is: a ligament joins bone to bone, a tendon joins muscle to bone.

base_tendon.description: The base model's tendon whose path seeds this rod at rest; absent for a rod the base model lacks (most ligaments).

via.description: Points the rod passes through at rest, in order from the first end, metres in the rest frame; empty for a straight rod.

parameters.description: The body parameters this anatomy has: each a physical quantity over part of the body, set per run (anatomy_run `selection.body`). A region-specific value (fat over the thigh, one muscle's volume) is one parameter per region.

id.description: The parameter's name, unique among the parameters; runs and results name it.

quantity.description: What the parameter sets, and so its unit: the scales, laxity and extensibility are ratios to the rest anatomy (unit 1; laxity > 1 is a laxer ligament, extensibility > 1 a more extensible skin), the thicknesses are metres.

bodies.description: Base-model bodies the parameter applies to (bone scales, ligament laxity at their joints).

rest_value.description: The value at which the anatomy is as authored: 1 for a ratio, the authored thickness for a thickness. A run that doesn't set the parameter solves at this value.

selection.description: An anatomy selects nothing: a run makes the choices.

references.description: Always empty: the base model is a payload, not a husk document, and runs and results reference the anatomy, not the other way round.

rod_end.description: Where a rod end is fixed: a point on a base-model body (body and point), or a tissue vertex (tissue and vertex), never both.

body.description: The base-model body the end is fixed to.

point.description: The end's position in the body's frame.

tissue.description: The tissue whose vertex the end is fixed to (a tendon's muscle end).

vertex.description: Index into that tissue's surface positions.
